decisions.reason: The FAQ already states that no-code rewards go to a random existing NFT holder, which is consistent with the clarified eligibility.
The source changes recipient eligibility only for mints without a referral code; coded-referral commission and ticket awards remain unchanged.
Changing the eligible recipient for no-code rewards does not change the requirement to display earned commissions and tickets in the dashboard.
The NFT mint number remains the permanent referral code regardless of who receives rewards when no code is supplied.
The same message reports a dashboard ownership-recording defect, but the no-code recipient eligibility change does not alter the dashboard ownership rule.
The no-code reward recipient eligibility change does not affect the independent requirement to display the complete NFT book cover.
The source identifies who may receive a no-code ticket but does not change ticket counters, eligibility windows, expiration, or post-draw behavior.
No-code reward recipient eligibility does not change the public accessibility or surfaces of aggregate referral statistics.
The source changes eligibility for receiving no-code commissions and tickets, not how prize winners are notified or paid.
Eligibility to receive a no-code referral reward does not alter the NFT-ownership requirement for ebook access.
The hero copy does not describe no-code reward recipient eligibility, so its current messaging remains valid unchanged.
The mechanics and prize-section copy covers coded referrals and prize frequency but does not state the no-code recipient eligibility rule.
